summaryBox.title: Conductance Equations
summaryBox.takeaway: G = 1/R; G* = l/A (cm⁻¹); κ = G·G* = G*/R (S/cm). Cell constant depends strictly on electrode geometry.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ELECTROLYTIC CONDUCTANCE EQUATIONS

• Resistance: R = ρ (l / A)  [Units: Ω]
• Conductance: G = 1 / R  [Units: Siemens (S) or Ω⁻¹]
• Cell Constant: G* = l / A  [Units: cm⁻¹ or m⁻¹]
• Conductivity (Specific Conductance): κ = 1 / ρ = G × G* = G* / R  [Units: S/cm or S·m⁻¹]
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Conductance ($G$)**: The reciprocal of electrical resistance ($G = 1/R$, in Siemens $\text{S}$).
• **Cell Constant ($G^* = l/A$)**: The geometric ratio of distance between electrodes ($l$) to their surface area ($A$). Unit: $\text{cm}^{-1}$ or $\text{m}^{-1}$.
• **Conductivity ($\kappa$)**: Conductance of a $1\text{ cm}^3$ cube of electrolytic solution: $\mathbf{\kappa = G \cdot G^* = \frac{G^*}{R}}$.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.2 Molar Conductivity (Λ_m) & Equivalent Conductivity (Λ_eq)
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Molar Conductivity (Λ_m) & Equivalent Conductivity (Λ_eq)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MOLAR & EQUIVALENT CONDUCTIVITY FORMULAS

• Molar Conductivity (Λ_m):
  Λ_m = (1000 × κ in S/cm) / M in mol/L  [Units: S·cm²/mol]

• Equivalent Conductivity (Λ_eq):
  Λ_eq = (1000 × κ in S/cm) / N in eq/L = Λ_m / n-factor  [Units: S·cm²/eq]
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Molar Conductivity ($\Lambda_m$)**: Conductance of a solution volume containing 1 mole of electrolyte placed between electrodes $1\text{ cm}$ apart: $\mathbf{\Lambda_m = \frac{1000 \cdot \kappa}{M}}$ (in $\text{S}\cdot\text{cm}^2\text{/mol}$).
• **Relation to $\Lambda_{eq}$**: $\Lambda_{eq} = \frac{\Lambda_m}{n\text{-factor}}$.
